description: Scrolling spectrogram: the frequency content of the input drawn against time, with a classic analysis and a time-frequency reassigned one, several colour palettes and a full-window view

params.text: Sets the quietest level the display shows, -140 to -40 dBFS; the top of the range is always 0 dBFS
Stops and starts the display without clearing what is on it
Erases the history and every marker on it
Sets how fast the history moves across the display: slower settings fit more time on screen, faster settings less

inputs.text: The left channel, or the whole signal when it is the only cable
The right channel; with no cable it takes the left input
A rise past 1V stops and starts the display, the same pause the FREEZE button gives
A rise past 1V drops a marker at the current point in the history

notes: hovering the display reads the frequency, the nearest note and the level under the pointer; shift and the wheel zoom the frequency range, dragging pans it, a double click resets it
changing the analysis mode clears the history, because rows from the two modes hold different measurements
the reassigned mode costs a good deal more processor time and holds each new row back by about one analysis window, though the timestamps it records refer to when the sound happened
the panel can be dragged wider or narrower, and the display grows with it
menu: Open expanded view — fills the Rack window with the running display, keeping its history; Space freezes and resumes it, Escape or a click outside closes it
Analysis mode: Classic, T-F Reassigned — Classic is the ordinary spectrogram; the reassigned one moves each piece of energy to its estimated true frequency and time
Channel mode: Left, Right, Mono, Mid, Side — chooses what is analysed; Mono averages the two inputs, or uses whichever one is connected on its own
FFT size: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — a larger size resolves frequency more finely and time more coarsely
FFT overlap: None, 25%, 50%, 75%, 87.5%, 93.75% — sets how far each analysis window overlaps the one before it
Window: Hann, Blackman-Harris, Flat-top — chooses the window function the analysis uses
Time detail: Economy · 15 rows/s, Normal · 30 rows/s, High · 60 rows/s — sets how many rows a second the display draws
Polyphonic voice: Channel 1 to Channel 16 — picks which channel of a polyphonic cable is analysed
Flow: Up, Down, Left, Right — sets the direction the history moves across the display
Palette — chooses the colours the levels are drawn in
Rendering: Precise, Smooth — chooses between drawing each bin exactly and smoothing between them
Trace: Live, Peak — sets the two optional traces drawn over the spectrogram
Ticks — turns the frequency and time guides on and off and sets how strong they are
Frequency — sets the axis labels, the smoothing, whether bins are spaced by Log, Linear or Mel, and resets the zoom
Markers — turns the markers on and off and sets how strong they are
